text:
emma: starting canary rollout for model service -> model: rwinfer-v2.9.1, weight-bundle: wb-202803, tokenizer: tk-202802 (2 hosts)

deploy-bot: canary rollout initiated by @emma — artifacts: wb-202803 / tk-202802 

monitoring-bot: [ALERT] canary latency spike on rwinfer-v2.9.1 (p90 420ms -> 1.9s)

levi-oncall: paging in case it's infra, looking now

raj: looking at inference logs on canary, seeing a ton of tokenization fallback warnings: "Unknown token sequence -> fallback to byte fallback"

oscar: that sounds like a tokenizer mismatch. which tokenizer did we ship?

emma: tk-202802, that matches the release notes. but weights were built against tk-202805 during CI? hmm

oscar: copy — I'm checking artifact metadata registry now

incident-bot: incident open: rwinfer-canary-tokenizer-mismatch (sev: p2). oncall: @levi-oncall. runbook: https://internal.runbooks/rwinfer/canary-tokenizer-mismatch

julia-cs: customer reports: "responses are truncated / gibberish" for a small subset of requests hitting canary — trying to correlate examples

raj: dumping sample inputs -> outputs from canary: ```Input: "Summarize Q1 results" -> Output: "� sum"``` definitely encoding/tokenization corruption

oscar: registry shows weights wb-202803 linked to tokenizer tk-202805 in model manifest. the deploy manifest referenced tk-202802 by mistake. artifact tag mismatch during promotion.

levi-oncall: candidate mitigations: 1) abort canary & rollback to previous model 2) flip kill-switch for model variant routing 3) hotpatch tokenizer on canaries. recommend immediate rollback to minimize customer impact.

emma: ACK. do rollback now, also alert CS.

deploy-bot: performing canary abort -> routing traffic back to rwinfer-v2.8.x. ETA ~60s

monitoring-bot: [INFO] traffic re-routed off canary; canary instances draining

julia-cs: confirming downstream customer visible errors dropping in Sentry for the affected customers, sending short note to a few impacted trial customers: "we briefly served a mismatched model on a small percentage of requests; we rolled it back and are investigating"

raj: I pulled the bad canary container image. artifact manifest shows promotion job used stale token. adding guard to promotion job to validate tokenizer hash against weight manifest.

oscar: opened PR to promotion pipeline to validate model manifest before promotion -> link: https://github.com/redwood/promote/pull/482

levi-oncall: flipping kill-switch flag for any future fast-rollouts to require explicit tokenizer-hash match: `POST /admin/flags/require_tokenizer_hash_match true` -> done

emma: creating postmortem ticket and customer impact summary. cc @julia-cs for customer followups.

incident-bot: incident severity reduced to p3 (no ongoing customer errors). incident owner: emma. next: collect canary samples, manifest diffs, and timeline.

julia-cs: posting a short advisory to impacted customers in the next 30m, will include apology and note about crediting any affected usage.

raj: note for follow-up: add a preflight check in runtime that verifies tokenizer-vocab checksum before serving any traffic for new variants. will prototype tomorrow.

oscar: also scheduling a quick run of the model-eval suite against promoted artifact tags in staging to catch tokenization regressions.

emma: thanks all. lessons: don't trust promotion tags; require manifest-level checksum equality.

monitoring-bot: [METRICS] canary error-rate returned to baseline. p90 latency normalizing.

incident-bot: incident closed (post-rollback monitoring in progress).
